summary: First-principles design review, iteration 11, fresh eyes on the campaign branch (full record in review_loop/scrutiny_11.md). The headline claim, confirmatory family, matching design, and SS0.1 framing were re-examined and stand. With the statistics stack twice re-derived defect-free (iterations 9-10), this pass audited the layer scrutiny had been thinnest on: the EVALUATION layer that turns patches into the resolved booleans every estimator consumes — checked against the installed SWE-bench harness SOURCE, not its assumed contract. Two major measurement-integrity holes found and fixed. (T1, major) The harness swallows ALL per-instance errors (EvaluationError, BuildImageError, bare Exception — run_evaluation.py:253-273) and writes no report; our eval driver mapped any missing report.json to resolved:false with exit 0 and wrote the trajectory_eval resume marker — so an eval-time Docker/build/container flake was silently scored as a genuine test failure, corrupting the Chen (n,c) in whichever arm it hit (can flip a per-instance any-pass, fabricate or destroy an R5.4 off-mode candidate), and the resume-marker skip froze the fabricated verdict forever; iteration 10's record even asserted the opposite ('eval steps fail loudly'). Fixed: missing reports are now CLASSIFIED from the harness's own logs — patch-apply failure and test timeout are patch-attributable failed draws recorded with fail_reason (SWE-bench convention), anything else raises EvalOutcomeError -> exit 3 WITHOUT writing the record (campaign retries once, then stops loudly). This deliberately does NOT extend the iteration-6/7 generation-layer symmetric-counting rule: at eval time the budget is spent, the patch exists with a definite ground-truth verdict, and the cause IS machine-distinguishable — recording false on a measurement failure is fabrication, not accounting. (T2, major) The harness returns an existing report.json keyed by (run_id, model, instance) WITHOUT re-evaluating (run_evaluation.py:118-123); our run_id was patch-content-blind, so re-evaluating after a treatment re-run inherited the PREVIOUS patch's verdict; fixed with patch_run_id (SHA-1 content hash in the run id: changed patch -> fresh verdict, identical patch -> legitimate cache reuse, making post-stop retries cheap), plus the harness's '/'->'__' model-name normalization mirrored in the report path (a slash-bearing model id would have silently scored a whole arm failed). Two consistency gaps also fixed: compare() now NAMES pred/eval draw-count desync (pred_eval_count_mismatch) instead of silently min()-ing inconsistent denominators across the H1/H2 endpoints, and the figure set gains the cross-arm-valid rarefied-distinct@k* chart (per-arm CIs at the common k*, H1 sign-flip p + power floor + H2 gate status printed on the figure) while the raw distinct bars are labeled own-k — the old figure invited exactly the mechanical sample-size comparison R4.2 forbids. R4.1 amended (applied_11_eval_outcome_integrity.md; tripwire-checked: adds obligations discharged same-iteration, flips nothing). 130 tests pass (121 -> 130, +9), py_compile clean, campaign dry-run plan correct, work committed (1cd3ed5). Because this iteration found and fixed real issues (two major), gold_standard_met is FALSE per the charter; the loop should make one more pass over the remaining unaudited third-party seams (dataset loader, NLI protocol) and the end-to-end doc chain.

issues_found.title: Eval-time infrastructure errors were silently scored as test failures: the SWE-bench harness swallows every per-instance error (apply-fail, timeout, Docker/build flakes) and writes no report, and the eval driver mapped missing report.json to resolved:false with exit 0 plus a resume marker — fabricating an unfalsifiable failed draw in whichever arm the flake hit
issues_found.rationale: Verified against the installed harness source (run_evaluation.py:253-273). Missing reports are now classified from the harness's own logs: patch-apply failure / test timeout = genuine patch-attributable failed draws with fail_reason; anything else raises EvalOutcomeError -> exit 3 without writing the record, so the campaign retries once then stops loudly. Distinct from the generation-layer symmetric-counting decision (iters 6-7): at eval time the budget is spent and the verdict is ground-truth-definite — scoring a measurement failure is fabrication. R4.1 amended; rejected alternatives in applied_11_eval_outcome_integrity.md.

issues_found.title: Stale-verdict reuse: the harness returns an existing report.json keyed by (run_id, model, instance) without re-evaluating, and the eval run_id was patch-content-blind — a re-run with a changed patch under the same trajectory id silently inherited the previous patch's verdict
issues_found.rationale: Verified at run_evaluation.py:118-123. patch_run_id embeds a SHA-1 of the patch content: changed patch -> fresh verdict; identical patch -> legitimate cache reuse (cheap retry after an infra stop). Model-name '/'->'__' normalization mirrored so a swapped model id cannot silently miss every report.

issues_found.title: The H1 rarefied loop silently absorbed predictions/eval draw-count disagreements via min(), so a desynced instance could have H1 and H2 computed at different k* with no trace in the artifact
issues_found.rationale: compare() now emits pred_eval_count_mismatch naming every disagreeing instance with both counts per arm, plus a console warning; empty list when consistent. Named-not-failed so the script stays usable for diagnosing partial artifacts.

issues_found.title: The figure script plotted raw per-arm distinct-patch counts side by side — the mechanical sample-size comparison R4.2 forbids cross-arm — and ignored the comparison block (rarefied levels, H1 inference, H2 gate) entirely
issues_found.rationale: Added fig_rarefied_distinct_at_k_star.png (per-arm rarefied levels + CIs at the common k*, annotated with H1 sign-flip p, min-achievable p, and the confirmatory_family H2 status) and labeled the raw distinct chart '(own k)'. The figure a reader grabs now states the same inference rule as the JSON.
